# Ecliptic Launcher · Beta 8

Safer imports, faster prepared pages, and a quieter launcher while Minecraft runs.

## Fixes

- New installations with an existing name automatically receive `(1)`, `(2)`, and so on. Names are allocated when saving, including imports in the same batch; editing an existing installation keeps its name.
- Imported launch profiles and client JARs use private internal IDs, so another launcher's version metadata cannot collide with or overwrite an existing installation.
- Shared libraries are reused only when their bytes match. Conflicting imported libraries get separate paths, and native-library classifiers are copied too.
- Copied loader profiles retain their exact launch configuration instead of being replaced by a generic loader installation.
- Imported installations keep their real Minecraft version in the UI and launch pipeline even when their internal launch IDs differ. Legacy Java selection and cosmetics hooks use the actual Minecraft version, with regression coverage for Java 8, 17, 21 and 25.
- World previews resolve imported client assets instead of assuming a matching vanilla client JAR already exists.
- Invalid imported library metadata returns an import error instead of crashing the operation.
- OptiFine's import confirmation uses the final saved installation name.

## Faster prepared pages

- The preloader prepares bundled artwork, fonts, page resources, saved installation contents, world thumbnails, server icons and account appearance through shared caches.
- Unchanged installation display snapshots survive restarts. Changed files trigger fresh inspection, while installation and launch integrity checks remain independent.
- Packaged images preload as compressed bytes, avoiding decoded copies of every offscreen background in RAM.
- Library and Addons share prepared inventories and installed-project artwork. History refreshes no longer discard those file caches.
- Optional previews, animations, polling and live-log repaints pause while a managed Minecraft game is running and the launcher is in the background. Returning to the launcher or exiting Minecraft wakes them; authentication, game monitoring and native logs continue.

## Before testing

This is a Windows x64 beta. Back up important worlds and test a fresh installation as well as an upgrade from Beta 6. Use **Ecliptic-Setup.exe** to install; component ZIPs are compiled updater payloads.

Imported source installations are retained. First-time or changed-file inspection can take longer than a warm start. New catalogue searches and live service data still need network access, and Java versions not already installed may download on first launch. Startup improvements do not guarantee a particular Minecraft FPS increase.
